common_topics.label: Current intent and outcome depth
common_topics.why: Distinguishes briefing, resumption, local change, tool construction and product execution.
questions: What do you need now: a new idea, continuation, clarification, repair, assessment or a change to the agent itself?
What result is due at the current stage, and where should work stop?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Recover the answer from the actual request and current state.

common_topics.label: Current sources, decisions and inherited context
common_topics.why: Preserves accepted intent and avoids asking the same questions again.
questions: Which supplied material is authoritative if the sources conflict?
What has already been accepted and needs to carry forward?
decisions: Current decisions, amendments and change impact
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Read available originals, current state, hashes and earlier replies first.

common_topics.label: Recipient, real situation and value
common_topics.why: Connects the result to an actual person, task and observable improvement.
questions: Who needs the result, and in what real situation?
How do they do this today, and what specifically should improve?
Who uses, pays for, operates and accepts the result?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Clarify separate roles only where they exist in the intended product.

common_topics.label: Full target, launch and confirming experiment
common_topics.why: Preserves ambition by separating production sequencing from scope reduction.
questions: What does the complete accepted result look like when realized?
What belongs in the first launch, and what belongs only in a separate experiment?
Which simplifications, substitutions or lost properties are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Bind a limited test to its own scope and retain the full target.

common_topics.label: Priorities, examples and counterexamples
common_topics.why: Turns quality expectations into domain requirements and early dependencies.
questions: What matters most in this idea, and why?
What concrete example is close to the desired outcome, and what exactly fits?
What would formally satisfy the request yet still be unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Preserve known examples and priorities verbatim with their source.

common_topics.label: Bounds, stage outcomes and dependencies
common_topics.why: Grounds planning in observed time and functional constraints.
questions: What deadlines, dependent events and required interim results already exist?
Which hard constraints, compatibility needs or external dependencies must stay in force?
Which decisions do you delegate to specialists, and which do you want to make yourself?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Use the actual authorized limits for hours, platforms and capabilities.

common_topics.label: Budget, time, available resources and tradeoffs
common_topics.why: Grounds a feasible route and the actual cost of achieving quality.
questions: What funds, time, devices, subscriptions, materials and help are already available?
Which one-off and recurring costs are acceptable, and which require a separate decision?
How should we choose among supported alternatives if current resources fall short of desired quality?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Verify uncertain prices when binding the actual operation.

common_topics.label: Materials, rights and preserved originals
common_topics.why: Establishes authority to use, modify and transfer the specific materials.
questions: Which existing text, design, code, brands, voices or other materials should be used?
What may be edited, generated, published or transferred, and who owns the rights?
Which originals or attribution must be preserved?
common_topics.applies_when: When input or generated materials are involved. Keep missing proof of rights open.

common_topics.label: Data, access, privacy and lifecycle
common_topics.why: Surfaces architecture requirements from sensitive or retained data early.
questions: What data is necessary, who controls it and who may see it?
What needs to be remembered, synced, exported or deleted?
Which consequences of loss, error or access revocation are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: When the result reads, creates or stores data. Review privacy even for minimal context.

common_topics.label: External actions, risk and owner participation
common_topics.why: Separates preparation from the exact external effect authorized.
questions: Which external actions are in scope: account changes, messages, publication, payments or service launch?
Which specific actions require your participation or a separate decision?
How should work stop, roll back and reconcile the actual result after interruption?
common_topics.applies_when: When external effects are possible. Reuse an exact valid grant.

common_topics.label: Host, available capabilities and handoff
common_topics.why: Makes execution and return of the actual result feasible.
questions: Where must the result operate, where do you manage it, and where should the package return?
Which hosts, tools, accounts and target devices have already been verified?
How should work move to another environment, and what should the recipient verify?
common_topics.applies_when: When tools, installation, execution or handoff are needed. Verify the actual operation in the named service.

common_topics.label: Acceptance, evidence and independent review
common_topics.why: Defines what demonstrates completion of the current stage.
questions: What behavior or artifact will you inspect to accept the result?
Which errors, boundary conditions and recovery situations must be demonstrated?
Where do we need an independent expert, real user, device or post-launch observation?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Verify domain quality and actual use independently of schema or checklist checks.

common_topics.label: Unknowns, research and future decisions
common_topics.why: Resolves material uncertainty through research and recommendations.
questions: Which decisions are still open and need research and a recommendation?
Which researched options fit your criteria, and do you accept the recommended option?
Which future parameters can be decided later, within what limits and by which milestone?
decisions: Deferred owner, baseline or range, due point and reopening condition
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Resolve every applicable material unknown before approving the execution plan.

topics.label: Participant's task and chatbot value
topics.why: Choose channel and technology for the actual task the participant needs to finish.
questions: Who needs the bot, in what situation, and what specific task should it carry through to an observable result?
How do people handle it today, how often does it arise, and what does an error or delay cost?
Which examples of acceptable and unacceptable results already exist?
topics.applies_when: For a new product or a change to its mission. Prefill confirmed intent for an existing bot from authoritative sources.

topics.label: Channels, audiences and roles
topics.why: Private, group and workspace contexts have different rights, experience and delivery.
questions: Where will people actually use the bot: privately, in a group, in a workspace, on a site or across verified channels?
Who is the owner, operator, member or guest, and must the same person be recognized in multiple channels?
Which channels have been selected or configured, and which should be compared and recommended using current capabilities?
topics.applies_when: For all new bots and changes to channels, access or membership.

topics.label: Complete solution and active systems
topics.why: Features work as one product with consistent obligations and state.
questions: What is the complete journey from initial request to actual result and later return?
Which capabilities are needed: answers from sources, personal memory, service actions, reminders, group interaction, media or others?
Should we compare end-to-end chatbot approaches with a simpler existing tool and recommend a route with verified tradeoffs?
topics.applies_when: Before specifying a new bot or major extension. Activate RAG, voice, games and multiple agents only when they meet a demonstrated need.

topics.label: Character and authority to act
topics.why: Tone, initiative and practical actions depend on people's expectations and permissions.
questions: What role and style fit: practical assistant, companion, facilitator or another role? Which examples sound appropriate?
When may it speak first, and when should it stay quiet, wait or hand off to a person?
Which actions can proceed immediately, require a specific person's decision, or lie outside its authority?
topics.applies_when: When introducing or changing behavior, especially in shared chats or where there can be external effects.

topics.label: Existing bot and capability preservation
topics.why: Development begins with the actual current product.
questions: Where are the current code, configuration, data, deployments and last working state?
Which existing capabilities, promises, style and integrations must be retained, and which problems should change?
Which outstanding actions, reminders, private data or older buttons must survive the update?
topics.applies_when: For an existing bot, targeted repair, migration or transfer. If an older agent package is unavailable, reconstruct from the code.

topics.label: Demand and economics relevant to the goal
topics.why: Validate cost, value people pay for and acquisition against the actual audience.
questions: Who already has this need, and how can we test usefulness with that audience?
For a paid proposal, what completed result would people pay for, and what current evidence supports that?
Do we need a subscription, payments, free access or another model? Which verified alternatives should inform the recommendation?
topics.applies_when: For new products, adoption or commercial changes. Service and personal bots need monetization only when it is part of the goal.

topics.label: People, needs and alternatives
topics.why: Research distinguishes desired outcomes from unvalidated demand.
questions: Which people and workflows are we studying, and what actual evidence can we access?
Which alternatives do they use, and when does a chatbot improve on them?
Which assumptions about frequency, trust, habits or willingness to pay should be tested first?
topics.applies_when: When the need, audience or advantage of conversation is unconfirmed.

topics.label: Channel feasibility
topics.why: Current official channel capabilities determine which promises are supportable.
questions: Which actions and message types does each intended channel require?
Which accounts, rights, installations and working environments are already accessible?
Which channels or adapters should be checked against official documentation and compared by delivery, limitations and cost?
topics.applies_when: For a new channel, changes in capability or permissions, or uncertain current support.

topics.label: Domain knowledge and evidence
topics.why: Reliable domain assistance needs authoritative data and defined limits of expertise.
questions: Which domain questions must the bot address, and who has authority over those rules?
Which documents, APIs, databases or specialists are available, how current are they, and who may use them?
Do professional, legal or other boundaries change what the bot can promise, how it verifies or when it hands off?
topics.applies_when: For a domain assistant, a knowledge workflow or a task where errors have material consequences.

topics.label: Actual tools and probes
topics.why: Verify the required operation independently of an integration's label.
questions: Which exact operations should the bot perform, and which tools or APIs are connected?
What can be verified with a read or a reversible isolated probe without external effects?
If an operation is unavailable, which verified alternatives and recommendation should we prepare?
topics.applies_when: For uncertain integrations, media generation, payments, automation or deployment.

topics.label: Constraints, costs and maintenance
topics.why: Choose a route with observable operating and maintenance costs.
questions: What volume, regions, languages, latency and availability do people require?
Which provider, hosting, model, media and platform costs can be measured, and which are estimates?
Which feasible architectures should we recommend based on full cost, privacy and portability?
topics.applies_when: When platform, model, media or scale choices affect budget or quality. Use verified limits.

topics.label: Research conclusion and open decisions
topics.why: A decision-ready recommendation identifies the limits of evidence.
questions: Which decisions need research before an execution plan can be approved?
Which claims have source evidence, which remain hypotheses, and what check would resolve them?
Is a bounded experiment needed, and which result would change the next choice?
topics.applies_when: At research closeout and before a material decision under incomplete evidence.

topics.label: Systems, data and events
topics.why: The specification assigns sources of truth and exact boundaries for every active capability.
questions: What entities, states, inputs, results and events does each accepted journey require?
Who is the single owner of the obligation, state and record of the result?
Which C1 architecture decisions are due now, and which numerical T details can wait within a named range and milestone?
decisions: C1 decisions and deferred T details
topics.applies_when: For each active system before implementation. Specialists prepare technical options and the owner decides material tradeoffs.

topics.label: Identity, audience and consent
topics.why: Sender and audience determine what the bot may read, remember or change.
questions: How do we identify person, tenant, workspace, chat and topic, and when may identities be linked?
Who can initiate, confirm, cancel or view each result?
How do join, leave, guest access, role change, revocation and private replies within a group workflow behave?
topics.applies_when: For any persistence or action. Group and multi-channel operation introduce additional boundaries.

topics.label: Complete action lifecycle
topics.why: User-visible success must reflect the real effect after retries or failures.
questions: Which actions move through proposal, clarification, authorization, execution, success, failure or unknown outcome?
What do cancellation before and after an external effect, partial success and restart recovery mean?
Which deduplication, retry, reconciliation, expiry and delivery rules match actual provider guarantees?
topics.applies_when: When the bot performs, schedules or delivers any action that takes time, may repeat or has an external effect.

topics.label: Time and scheduling
topics.why: People act in civil time, which may differ from the server's timezone.
questions: Which one-time or recurring events are needed, and in whose time zone?
How should the bot handle clock changes, lateness, missed runs, schedule changes or user silence?
When does a reminder become stale, and who can change or revoke its rule?
topics.applies_when: When reminders, proactive events, deadlines or other time-dependent behavior apply.

topics.label: Memory, knowledge and erasure
topics.why: Personal facts and domain documents have different sources, rights and lifetimes.
questions: What may the bot remember at session, task, person, group or workspace scope?
What can it store, how can errors be corrected, how long is retention, and how do people view, export and erase data?
Which derived summaries, indexes, caches, jobs and backups inherit corrections and revocation?
topics.applies_when: When memory, documents, retrieval or stored results are in scope. Record a reason when the capability is unnecessary.

topics.label: System interactions and acceptance
topics.why: Failures often occur between individually correct components.
questions: Which dependencies connect conversation, authorization, memory, scheduler, media, providers and delivery?
How should version conflicts, forget during execution, stale buttons, cross-chat requests and partial failures behave?
Which positive and negative scenarios establish the accepted rules across the full journey?
topics.applies_when: For every active cross-system dependency before build or a material shared-contract change.

topics.label: Role, voice and real dialogue examples
topics.why: Evaluate naturalness through appropriate utterances using context and audience.
questions: How should the bot sound in work, friendly, emotional and failure situations, and which existing replies feel appropriate or off-putting?
Which languages, forms of address, humor and cultural conventions are needed?
Which limits on role, expertise and personal claims must the persona preserve?
topics.applies_when: When creating or changing a persona. Keep the accepted voice and refine the affected parts.

topics.label: Addressee, turn-taking and appropriate silence
topics.why: In a group, determine which turns actually authorize or invite a response.
questions: How do people address the bot and each other, or return to a prior topic?
When is a reply, brief clarification, wait, silence or human handoff appropriate?
How should pause, a direct new task after pause, two active offers and an ambiguous “go ahead” («давай») work?
topics.applies_when: For conversational interaction, especially group, ambient or proactive use.

topics.label: Complete interaction grammar
topics.why: People need understandable entry, choice, cancellation and return across the whole journey.
questions: How does someone start, discover capabilities, supply data, inspect details, change their decision, cancel and return?
Where are text, commands, buttons, forms, voice or another demonstrated channel capability appropriate?
Which input forms fit user effort and accessibility given the selected platform's constraints?
topics.applies_when: For each journey. Choose the number of steps and input forms from the actual interaction needs.

topics.label: Accurate progress and recovery
topics.why: A success message needs evidence of the corresponding result.
questions: What should people see during preparation, queueing, execution, delivery, partial failure and an unknown outcome?
What useful next action fits when access, data or capability is missing?
How should the system preserve an accepted independent part when another part requires clarification or repair?
topics.applies_when: When replies depend on tools, jobs, state or unavailable capabilities.

topics.label: Shared activities and voluntary participation
topics.why: Each involved participant retains their own consent.
questions: Which shared tasks or activities are needed, and who can invite, join, decline and leave?
Are private roles, individual choices, vote threshold, unanimous consent, timeout or late join needed?
What is the first meaningful step, how does return after pause work, and what happens when someone declines or drops out?
topics.applies_when: For collaborative workflows, group decisions or games. Use game mechanics only where they serve the intended activity.

topics.label: Languages, length and accessibility
topics.why: The experience must work in the actual channel and support the audience's ways of accessing it.
questions: Which languages, locales and accessibility needs apply to the actual audience?
How should long results, tables, attachments, transcripts and media appear in each channel?
Which examples establish appropriate depth for a simple turn, complex explanation, failure and recovery?
topics.applies_when: For supported languages, media or constrained clients. Keep necessary content in complex tasks.

topics.label: Conversation experience evaluation
topics.why: Model scores and human perception require distinct evidence.
questions: Which frozen contexts and real kinds of turns represent the intended experience?
Which mistakes matter most: unwanted reply, silence, wrong addressee, repeated question, lost task or others?
Who can voluntarily review naturalness, and should comparisons allow a “both are poor” judgment?
topics.applies_when: For quality claims or persona and router changes. Require applicable authorization to use private production dialogue.

topics.label: Memory scopes and writes
topics.why: Preserve the meaning of the fact and the limits of its origin.
questions: Which facts are needed for a session, task, person, group and workspace, and who may write them?
How do we distinguish a direct remember request from a quotation, guess, denial or temporary preference?
Which automatic and explicit writes fit the data and consequences of an error?
decisions: Consent and lifetime of a fact
topics.applies_when: When memory is active. Add long-term profiling only when required.

topics.label: Corrections and conflicting knowledge
topics.why: An authoritative correction takes precedence over a later summary.
questions: Who may correct a fact, how is source authority determined, and when does information become stale?
How should the bot handle conflicting sources, unclear identity or a low-confidence inference?
How can someone view and correct what the bot stored about them?
topics.applies_when: For stored facts or multiple sources that may conflict.

topics.label: Retrieval for an actual domain need
topics.why: Select a search method from the questions and data it must serve.
questions: Which questions should the bot answer, from which corpora, and what counts as correct?
Do current context, ordinary search or SQL suffice, and if needed, which verified retrieval options should be compared?
How are sources updated, cited, filtered by access and deleted?
topics.applies_when: When access to external knowledge is required. Adopt a vector database only if justified by the retrieval task.

topics.label: Privacy, forgetting and derived data
topics.why: Forgetting also covers the derivatives of the deleted source.
questions: Which data is private, and for which audiences and purposes may it be used?
What must follow a “forget” request («забудь»), access revocation, role change or expiry?
Which actual backup, export, embedding, cache and running-job rules support that promise, and what needs a separate decision?
topics.applies_when: For any stored or derived data, including messages and media.

topics.label: Knowledge evidence and migration
topics.why: Evaluate retrieval, answers and erasure independently.
questions: Which authorized frozen question set tests relevance, citation correctness, abstention and rights?
Which parser, model, ACL, index or schema changes require reindexing or renewed evaluation?
How do migration and restore preserve corrections, expiry and tombstones?
topics.applies_when: For active knowledge stores, memory or changes to their dependencies.

topics.label: Adapter for each channel
topics.why: Verify each channel's actual APIs and rights independently.
questions: Which events, callbacks, message types, threads, groups and delivery modes does each channel require?
Which transport signatures, scopes, rate limits, ACK and delivery guarantees do current authoritative sources support?
Which supported adapter options fit, and what gaps remain?
topics.applies_when: For each selected channel and changes to affected operations. Use the contract for the actual platform.

topics.label: Accounts, credentials and authority
topics.why: Verify authorization for each external effect within an accessible service.
questions: Whose accounts and workspaces does the bot use, and which rights are actually granted?
Do actions use the person's, bot's or shared service's identity, and how is access linked and revoked?
Which actions need specific confirmation, and how do we reuse an existing valid grant for the same scope?
topics.applies_when: For external services, private resources, administrative or delegated actions.

topics.label: Specific tools and outcomes
topics.why: Each action has actual parameters, cost and completion evidence.
questions: Which reads and mutations does the full journey need, and what are their inputs and outputs?
Which parameters, limits, current prices, editable outputs and cancellation does each provider support?
Which evidence establishes effect, provider acceptance, delivery or preparation alone?
topics.applies_when: For each required operation, including media, documents, search, automation and payments.

topics.label: Retries, cancellation and uncertainty
topics.why: After an external timeout, reconcile whether the action took effect.
questions: What does the provider support for idempotency, status or readback, cancel, reconciliation and compensation?
How should the system handle a duplicate event, crash between send and commit, timeout after success, or partial response?
What retry bounds, deadlines and separation of chat and job workers fit the actual guarantees?
topics.applies_when: When an operation can repeat, run long, incur cost or create an external effect.

topics.label: Schedules and proactive actions
topics.why: Scheduling preserves civil-time intent, the authorization version and unique occurrences.
questions: Which reminders or recurring actions are explicitly requested, and who receives them?
How do reschedule, revoke, quiet hours, DST, restart, missed or expired occurrences work?
Which available scheduler will perform this, and which evidence verifies the rule was created?
topics.applies_when: For authorized future or repeated actions. Verify actual automation creation before claiming the schedule exists.

topics.label: Payments and fulfillment
topics.why: Keep the financial event and entitlement to the result consistent.
questions: If payments are in scope, what is purchased, in which currency and through which verified provider?
Which entitlement, refund, dispute, tax or accounting rules apply to this product?
How do duplicate webhooks, payment uncertainty, cancellation and partial fulfillment avoid double fulfillment?
topics.applies_when: When payments or monetary effects are explicitly in scope. Use qualified expertise for applicable legal and financial choices.

topics.label: Media purpose and placement
topics.why: Each media item should advance an intended user outcome.
questions: For which specific moments are images, stickers, animation, voice, music or video needed?
What does the bot create at runtime, and what can be prepared in advance?
Which accepted quality examples and unwanted styles exist, and which available approaches fit the selected channel?
topics.applies_when: For each required media component. A single preview defines only the demonstrated scope.

topics.label: Identity, voice and rights
topics.why: Preserve identity continuity and use rights from source through delivery.
questions: Which identity, character, brand or voice is needed, and which references may be used?
Who owns source material, licenses and rights to adapt, generate and publish?
Which changes to identity, pronunciation, emotion or style are unacceptable?
topics.applies_when: For branded, character, voice or third-party materials.

topics.label: Formats and channel delivery
topics.why: A valid local file also needs to work in the actual client.
questions: Which channels, devices and message types will display each item?
What are the current dimensions, alpha, duration, codecs, file size, frame timing, loop, captions and audio stream requirements?
Which editable originals, exports, manifests, order and readback does the recipient need?
topics.applies_when: For each active media type and channel. Verify exact settings against current sources.

topics.label: Voice and accessible alternatives
topics.why: Audio needs meaningful content, intelligible pronunciation and accessible text.
questions: Which languages, voice roles, pronunciation, emotions, pace and interaction do people need?
Are speech input, TTS, realtime interruption, transcripts, captions or a text equivalent needed?
Which verified voice options should be auditioned and recommended given rights, latency and cost?
topics.applies_when: When voice, audio or an accessibility requirement is active.

topics.label: Generation, jobs and resource limits
topics.why: Media production needs an integrated route to the result in chat.
questions: Which operations and transformations are needed from input to usable media in the actual client?
Which representative item will measure real time, cost and quality before the catalog expands?
How do people see progress, cancel long work and get recovery after partial or unknown delivery?
topics.applies_when: For generation or a large media catalog. Keep the agreed final scope while measuring the slice.

topics.label: Validation of the claimed media scope
topics.why: Movement, sound and set membership each need corresponding evidence.
questions: Which assets, motions, audio tracks and states are in acceptance scope?
What checks are needed for decode, loop, content, identity, accessibility, runtime import and platform membership?
Who evaluates creative fit, and which properties are established by files, playback or actual readback?
topics.applies_when: For a created, changed or published media catalog.

topics.label: Code, environment and change contract
topics.why: A reproducible baseline helps distinguish the needed change from accidental regression.
questions: Which repository, branch, source version, toolchains, configuration and environment are authoritative?
Which active capabilities, tests, data and assets must carry forward, and what exactly changes?
What input and acceptance criteria does implementation receive from each active module?
topics.applies_when: Before changing code or resuming an existing product.

topics.label: Feasible implementation
topics.why: Fit the technology to the accepted architecture and actual capabilities.
questions: Which accepted privacy, latency, scale, portability and maintenance needs determine the architecture?
Which available languages, frameworks, storage, SDKs and hosting options fit after verification?
Which material tradeoffs still need an owner decision, and which implementation details are delegated?
topics.applies_when: When a new implementation or architectural change affects the outcome. Adopt queues, Redis or vector services only for a demonstrated need.

topics.label: Real journey and complete scope
topics.why: An integrated slice proves boundaries early in production of the accepted scope.
questions: Which representative path runs from platform event through permissions and state to provider effect and scoped delivery?
Which remaining journeys, catalogs and states belong to the full accepted result?
Where does real integration end and simulation begin, and what evidence closes each required external boundary?
topics.applies_when: For a new capability or integration. Keep the accepted full product scope alongside the slice.

topics.label: Failure, data and recovery
topics.why: Implement lifecycle reliability with normal behavior.
questions: Which guards are needed for duplicates, stale callbacks, wrong actors, cancellation, expiry, revocation, forget and restart?
How do migrations, backup and restore, version fences and privacy tombstones preserve current state?
How can long jobs and simple replies run separately while preserving required capabilities within resource limits?
topics.applies_when: For active state, persistence or external jobs. Specialists design the details within the accepted rules.

topics.label: Meaningful tests and observability
topics.why: Prove behavior and capture causal traces without leaking data.
questions: Which build, static, type, integration and negative checks fit the risk?
Which identifiers, outcomes, timing and cost are needed for diagnosis, and which data must be redacted?
What raw evidence package should independent QA receive, including actual commands and open proof boundaries?
topics.applies_when: Before implementation closes. Choose tests that exercise meaningful behavior and repeat passing checks when there is a new reason.

topics.label: Reproducibility and implementation handoff
topics.why: The recipient should run and verify the result without chat history.
questions: Which sources, assets, config examples, migrations, fixtures, CI and run commands does the recipient need?
Which secrets or external dependencies must the recipient provide through an appropriate channel?
Which readiness and blockers have been verified, and what action can proceed next?
topics.applies_when: At implementation closeout or when handing off to another host or operator.

topics.label: Independent inputs and exact scope
topics.why: Review the concrete artifact and requirements independently from the author's account.
questions: Which frozen source, build, assets, configuration, models, environment and requirement IDs are under review?
Which active or unchanged capabilities are transitively affected, and which evidence can legitimately carry forward?
Who performs independent QA and final acceptance without a conflict with authorship?
topics.applies_when: For any QA claim, especially on shared or critical changes.

topics.label: Authority, privacy and accurate claims
topics.why: Keep a blocking failure separate from aggregate scores.
questions: Which checks verify DM, group and tenant isolation, actual consent and the exact destination of delivery?
How can we reproduce revoke or forget during execution, stale source, old restore and derived caches or exports?
Which evidence gaps remain for actual provider effect, human consent and delivery?
topics.applies_when: For active data, groups, tools, memory or external effects.

topics.label: Reliability and cross-system failure
topics.why: Real failures often pass through multiple components.
questions: Which duplicates, cancellation before or after dispatch, timeout after success, partial failures, crash or restart and version races need reproduction?
How should DST, reschedule, resource exhaustion, queue delay and uncertain delivery be tested for active capabilities?
Which traces distinguish correct recovery from a hidden duplicate effect or lost task?
topics.applies_when: For active dependencies involving state, time, jobs or providers.

topics.label: Conversation and knowledge
topics.why: Relevance, retrieval and factual accuracy need distinct test sets.
questions: Which frozen contexts exercise direct, indirect, human-to-human, playful, pause, ambiguous, failed and resumed dialogue?
How will we measure unwanted speech or silence, wrong referent, repeated questions, lost work and localization with denominators?
Which separate tests are needed for knowledge ACL, citation, relevance, factuality and abstention, and voluntary human review of naturalness?
topics.applies_when: For relevant active conversation and knowledge capabilities. Record why a stratum is inapplicable.

topics.label: Actual client and media
topics.why: Display, sound and channel membership require evidence on the target boundary.
questions: Which actual platforms, clients and devices need smoke and end-to-end checks?
Which frozen media files, motion, audio streams, loops, captions, manifests and fingerprints need verification?
Which results prove actual readback, acceptance, delivery or preparation alone?
topics.applies_when: For selected platforms and active media. An unavailable live boundary blocks its corresponding claim.

topics.label: Findings, repair and acceptance
topics.why: Findings need to be reproducible and usable for targeted repair.
questions: Which finding IDs, severity, expected and actual results, reproduction, raw evidence and strongest objections does the recipient need?
Which items are reported, reproduced, hypotheses or preferences, and which targeted retest would close each change?
Which scoped GO, NO-GO or unknown follows from evidence, and which dependent milestones remain blocked?
topics.applies_when: At review closeout. A critical unknown remains open when time or budget runs out.

topics.label: Exact release target and authority
topics.why: Match external action to the verified artifact, target and current grant.
questions: Which account, platform, service, environment, source or build and asset versions, and rollout scope are the target?
Which deploy, publication, paid resource or migration actions already have authority?
What reversible preparation and readiness checks are due before a decision on any remaining unauthorized action?
topics.applies_when: For external release. Reuse exact valid authority and resolve material unknowns before execution approval.

topics.label: Compatibility with current obligations
topics.why: Preserve pending jobs, older buttons and privacy rules through the update.
questions: Which pending jobs, callbacks, semantic versions, schemas, models, credentials and media fingerprints must survive?
How do we verify backwards compatibility, retention and tombstones for current users?
Which migrations are forward-only, and which consequences need a material decision?
topics.applies_when: For updates to an existing bot or data. Specify supported contracts for new products too.

topics.label: Rollback, recovery and stop
topics.why: The release plan identifies when and how to recover a verified state.
questions: What is the safe rollout, stop condition, health check and owner of the stop decision?
How do we test backup, restore and rollback in isolation without reviving erased data?
Where are compensation or forward repair required because an external effect cannot be verifiably reversed?
topics.applies_when: For deployment, data migration or publication that affects current people or services.

topics.label: Actual receipts and live verification
topics.why: Deployment, provider acceptance and user delivery are distinct events.
questions: Which deploy or publication IDs, pinned versions, hashes, times, environments and raw receipts are recorded?
Which bounded platform smoke and readback verify the released capability and required media?
How do we reconcile an uncertain response before resubmitting a job or publication?
topics.applies_when: During an authorized actual release. Exercise the live path even when CI passed.

topics.label: Operator and post-release commitments
topics.why: Support and recovery need a named owner.
questions: Who receives alerts, support requests, unknown jobs, cost events and privacy requests?
Which current runbooks, contacts, evidence limits, service commitments, exports and recovery steps does the operator need?
Which recurring monitoring is authorized to create, and which remains a proposal?
topics.applies_when: At release closeout or transfer to another host or operator.

topics.label: State, symptoms and causal repair
topics.why: Use current receipts and reproduction to establish the incident.
questions: What is the observed symptom, who is affected, when did it begin, and what recent changes or unfinished obligations are known?
Which source, provider, configuration and model versions and current traces are available?
What is the smallest check that distinguishes leading hypotheses, and what current functionality must the repair preserve?
topics.applies_when: For a defect, incident or degradation in an existing bot.

topics.label: Reliability and privacy-safe observability
topics.why: Measure completed outcomes as well as message volume.
questions: Which actual completions, failures, unknowns, duplicates, queue age, latency, cost and resource metrics does the operator need?
Which SLIs, SLOs or alerts match the actual service commitment, and which denominators and baselines support them?
How can diagnostics avoid private transcripts, credentials and cross-audience disclosure?
topics.applies_when: For committed operating duties or diagnostic needs. State what data and monitoring actually exist.

topics.label: Cost, quotas and degradation
topics.why: When quotas are exceeded, communicate what the bot can do and keep its state recoverable.
questions: What actual provider, model, media and hosting costs and quota trends are known?
Which degradation options preserve accepted capabilities, and what tradeoffs should be recommended to the owner?
Which budget, plan, quality or provider changes need a new material decision?
topics.applies_when: When actual cost or quota applies. Check authority for upgrades, caps or disabling a capability.

topics.label: Evolution with valid evidence
topics.why: A model, prompt, provider or data change can affect several journeys.
questions: What need or regression should the change address, and which current commitments apply?
Which dependent evals, reviews, schemas, media or knowledge claims does the exact diff invalidate?
Which unaffected evidence can carry forward, and what scoped QA and rollout are needed?
topics.applies_when: For evolution, dependency changes or product transfer.

topics.label: Support and user value
topics.why: Feedback needs a responsible route, and adoption needs observable value.
questions: How do people ask for help, report issues and see case status?
Who may receive escalations, and what contacts, SLAs and external messages are authorized?
What usage and dissatisfaction evidence would help improve onboarding or core value?
topics.applies_when: For support of an existing product. Confirm exact authorization for email or broadcasts.

topics.label: Continuity, portability and retirement
topics.why: Preserve the owner's control of product and data across operator changes or shutdown.
questions: How do we verify backup, restore, export, portability and replacement of the operator or host?
What happens to jobs, reminders, access, payments and private data when paused or shut down?
What retention, deletion, deprecation notices and final handoff fit the current commitment?
topics.applies_when: For operational readiness, migration, ownership change or service closure.
